D: A Paris-trained dressmaker comes home to the dusty Victorian town that ran her out as a child, and dresses it up for revenge.
P: Pass the party pies when Tilly turns up at the footy in red.
S: CWA tasty cheese scones with butter
Light tasty cheese scones, split warm and buttered, for the fete tea table.

Rub 50g cold butter into 450g self-raising flour and 1 tsp salt, stir in 150g grated tasty cheese, then mix in about 300ml cold milk with a butter knife to a soft, sticky dough. Pat out to 3cm thick, cut into 12 rounds, set close together on a tray and brush with milk. Bake at 220C for 15 minutes until risen and golden, and serve warm with butter.
Asparagus rolled in soft buttered bread, for Gertrude's dress at the footballers dance

Blanch the asparagus in salted boiling water for 2 minutes, then plunge into iced water and pat dry. Beat the butter with the lemon zest, chives and pepper. Cut the crusts off the bread and roll each slice thin with a rolling pin. Spread with the butter, lay a spear across each slice, roll up tightly and cut in half.
Poached chicken set in clear jelly, sliced cold with salad and pickles.

Simmer a 1.6kg chicken with 1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick and 2 bay leaves in 1.5 litres of water for 45 minutes, then cool in the stock for 20 minutes. Pick the meat into chunks. Strain 500ml of the stock, whisk in 4 tsp gelatine softened in cold water until dissolved, and stir in 2 tbsp chopped parsley. Pack the chicken into a lined loaf tin, pour over the stock and chill at least 3 hours. Turn out and serve sliced with lettuce, tomato and pickled onions.
M: Sergeant Farrat's chicken a la king vol-au-vents
Creamy chicken à la king in vol-au-vents. Farrat takes a feather boa as a bribe.

Brown the chicken in the butter, then lift it out. Cook the mushrooms and capsicum in the same pan until soft. Stir in the flour, then the stock and cream, and simmer until it coats a spoon. Return the chicken with the peas and tarragon and simmer until cooked through. Warm the cases at 180C for 5 minutes, fill generously and serve.
Wedding breakfast roast lamb with mint sauce
Roast lamb with fresh mint sauce, for Gertrude's wedding breakfast with William Beaumont

Stir the sugar into the boiling water, add the vinegar and mint and set the mint sauce aside. Cut small slits in the lamb, push in the garlic and rosemary, rub with oil and season well. Roast at 180C for 1 hour 20 minutes for pink, adding the potatoes and pumpkin for the last hour. Rest the lamb for 20 minutes while the potatoes crisp up at 220C. Carve and serve with the vegetables and mint sauce.
W: Molly's chocolate brownies with wattleseed cream
Fudgy chocolate brownies with wattleseed cream, Molly's brownies for Irma's arthritis

Melt the chocolate and butter together over low heat, then cool a little. Whisk in the sugar, eggs and vanilla, then fold in the flour, cocoa and a pinch of salt. Pour into a lined 20cm tin and bake at 170C until just set, with a fudgy middle. Whip the cream with the wattleseed and icing sugar and serve on the cooled brownies.
K: Paris via Melbourne raspberry champagne cocktail
Raspberry purée topped with Champagne, for Tilly's train to Paris via Melbourne
Simmer the raspberries, sugar and water for 5 minutes, then push through a sieve and chill. Drop a sugar cube and a spoonful of syrup into each flute. Top slowly with the cold sparkling and serve.
